sensory.aromaNotes: Historic Pekilo product was a bland, protein-rich powder or biomass rather than a fruiting-body food
sensory.meatAnalogRationale: Pekilo was a full-scale Finnish single-cell protein process in the 1970s; modern work revisits the strain as a circular mycoprotein from residual sugars.
sensory.preparationContext: Submerged fermentation biomass; historically used as feed protein, with renewed food-SCP interest
sensory.confidenceNotes: Sensory of a modern food-grade ingredient is not well published; scores are conservative.

morphology.fruitingBodyStructure: No food fruiting body; identification is by culture and microscopy, not a mushroom
morphology.sporeCharacteristics: Smooth phialoconidia in long dry chains; no canoe-shaped Fusarium macroconidia
morphology.microscopyNotes: Irregularly branched conidiophores; phialides elongated and tapering (flask-to-awl). Distinct from Fusarium (macroconidia) and Aspergillus (vesicle). Pekilo literature uses the name P. variotii; the species complex has been revised.

nutrition.limitingAminoAcids: Sulfur amino acids (typical of fungal SCP)
nutrition.preparationContext: Historic Pekilo biomass was a high-protein SCP from spent sulfite liquor
nutrition.confidenceNotes: Protein range from process literature; attach a primary proximate table before using in formulation specs.

geographic.habitat: Soil, compost, and industrial residual streams

strains.availabilityNotes: Confirm the Pekilo production strain accession before citing a catalog number.

images.caption: Paecilomyces variotii in culture (the Pekilo organism)

commercialUse.applicationSummary: Pekilo was an industrial SCP process in Finland; not a current mainstream retail meat analog, but it is a documented mycoprotein platform on residual sugars.

companies.name: Historic Pekilo mills (Tampella / Finnish pulp industry)

productionProcess.title: Submerged fermentation on residual sugars
productionProcess.description: Continuous culture on spent sulfite liquor or other sugar streams; biomass dried as protein.

commercialUse.confidenceNotes: Historic commercial SCP; current food-grade status must be checked per jurisdiction.

regulatory.notes: Historic feed/SCP use in Finland. Do not treat as an authorized novel food without checking the current dossier.

altProteinResearch.title: A life cycle environmental sustainability analysis of microbial protein production via the Pekilo process
altProteinResearch.summary: Revisits Pekilo as a circular microbial protein route and frames environmental performance versus other protein systems.
